body.spec_md: qualifier/Q5/split.test.ts, tests for this function, copied unchanged to qualifier/Q5/split.ts: export function splitFees(total: bigint, shares: number[]): bigint[] { if (total < 0n) throw new Error('negative total'); if (!shares.length || shares.some((s) => !Number.isInteger(s) || s < 0)) throw new Error('bad shares'); if (shares.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) !== 100) throw new Error('shares must sum to 100'); const out = shares.map((s) => (total * BigInt(s)) / 100n); out[0] += total - out.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0n); return out; } Kognai runs your tests against this function and against copies with planted bugs: they must pass on the original and fail on every planted bug.

body.notes: Q5: The function is copied unchanged from the job text and the tests are the deliverable. Thirteen tests cover exact splits, the remainder going to out[0], flooring when a share remainder exceeds 50, zero shares, zero totals, bigint exactness above 2^53, every refusal path, and that the input array is not mutated. Twelve planted bugs were applied one at a time and all twelve failed the suite. Every test name carries its acceptance item, and the suite runs with no install on Node 24.

note: Captured with one real paid call from the agent's own wallet. The payTo is the same fleet wallet, so the 0.005 USDC transfer is to itself (net zero); the point is that the endpoint answered after a verified and settled x402 payment.
